title: Geo-claim aggregator and tenant isolation snapshot
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a verifiable, on-demand package of per-tenant residency and isolation state for dedicated capacity customers that auditors and security teams can pull or receive on schedule. The package must prove the mapping of tenant routing, node pool allocation, network egress boundaries, and retention policy application at a point-in-time.

Scope:
- Produce cryptographically-signed residency snapshots (JSON) that include tenant -> node assignments, region tags, active ingress/egress IPs, and retention policy markers.
- Implement a chain-of-custody reporter that appends sequential snapshot metadata (timestamp, signer id, signature, snapshot hash) and exposes a compact verification object (Merkle root + per-tenant leaf proofs).
- Provide an auditor-facing pull API (OAuth-protected) and an S3 export flow for scheduled deliveries.
- Integrate signing using customer-specific KMS keys when requested and platform HSM KMS for default signing.
- Include redaction and PII-hashing rules so snapshots do not leak secrets while still enabling verification.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term archival UI in Console, support for on-prem private control plane in air-gapped mode (follow-up ticket), and automated legal attestation language. Those will be handled in subsequent work items.

Non-goals: Replace existing ledger experiments—this is a pragmatic, audit-first snapshoter designed for our Dedicated customers and compliance audits, not a full public tamper-proof ledger product.
acceptance_criteria: Signed snapshot JSON can be generated for a tenant and includes tenant id, node pool id, region, active node IDs, ingress/egress CIDR list (redacted where necessary), retention policy id and effective window.
Each snapshot is accompanied by a compact verification object (Merkle root + leaf proof) and the platform HSM-signed assertion digest.
Auditor pull API: authenticated endpoint returns snapshots for a requested time range with proper ACL checks and rate limits; API calls are logged to audit logs with requestor identity.
Scheduled export job can deposit zipped evidence packages to a configured S3 destination with integrity checks (SHA256) and lifecycle TTL matching the customer's retention settings.
Snapshots reference the exact config versions (git commit refs for routing/orchestration) so reviewers can reconcile config drift.
Automated unit and integration tests covering signer rotation, redaction rules, and verification proof validation run in CI with >90% coverage for the core modules.
Documentation: PRD and runbook describing how to request and validate snapshots, KMS onboarding steps, and expected SLAs for ad-hoc vs scheduled requests.
No sensitive keys or raw customer secrets are included in the snapshot; all secrets are replaced with stable hashed placeholders.

implementation_notes: Schema versioning: start with v1.0 and include a schema_version field in every snapshot. Avoid breaking changes—add fields behind feature flags.
Signing: use AWS KMS/EKMS HSM for platform default key; allow tenant-specific KMS ARN to be supplied during Dedicated onboarding. Use RSA-PSS or ECDSA with SHA256.

Merkle tree: canonicalize JSON leaf ordering before hashing. Use SHA256 for leaf and node hashing. Store per-leaf proofs in evidence bundle to allow auditors to verify a single tenant's claim without full snapshot ingestion.
Retention enforcement: evidence packages must include retention_policy_id and computed expiration timestamp for the package; export lifecycle on S3 must respect that TTL.
Redaction: replace IPs deemed sensitive with hashed tokens using HMAC-SHA256 with a platform salt stored in KMS; keep stable mapping for traceability without revealing raw values.
Operational controls: add an async job to reconcile snapshots with runtime routing state every 6 hours; failures create alert to SRE with runbook link.
CLI tooling: residency-report generate --tenant <id> --at <timestamp> to produce local verifiable package for engineering troubleshooting.
test_plan: Unit tests for snapshot serializer and canonicalization (edge cases: empty node lists, multi-region tenants).
Integration test: end-to-end snapshot generation, sign with test KMS key, verify proof locally using verifier binary in CI.
Security tests: redaction verification that no raw IPs or secrets are present in artifacts; key rotation simulation test.
Load test: scheduled export pipeline must handle 2000 tenants/day without exceeding export window; simulate export batching and S3 writes.
Pen test checklist for auditor API: rate limit bypass, authentication spoofing, and data exfiltration scenarios (coordinate with SecOps).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Snapshot may accidentally include sensitive data. Mitigation: strict redaction library + CI hook that scans artifacts for raw secrets before release.
Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: KMS HSM, quarterly rotation, and immediate revocation flow plus re-signing plan for recent snapshots.
Risk: Auditor API misuse or excessive load. Mitigation: strong auth (OAuth2), rate limits, requestor whitelisting, and usage billing/backpressure.
Risk: Snapshot vs actual state drift. Mitigation: reconcile job, config version references, and embedding of routing commit hashes to reconcile with git history.
